messages.subject: Welcome to Rattle
messages.body_plain:
Rattle is an open source project that aims to bring the power of the
open source R project to the general user for Data Mining.

This discussion group will allow users to share experiences and to
discuss future development.

Please use the issues tracker of the package to report bugs and suggest
changes.

messages.subject: Rattle on OSX
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I'm having a great deal of woe getting rattle up and running on my
ibook running Tiger 10.4.6. Here's the deal:

I installed GTK2 2.8.19 via darwinports and then RGtk2 2.8.9.
I next downloaded and installed rattle via an R session in X11 (GTK2
will not load in the standard 'Aqua' OSX environment).

Great.

Except when i try to start rattle via library(rattle) I get nothing.
RGtk2 gets loaded and i'm returned to the R prompt as though rattle had
loaded but there is no display that I can see.

I've tried poking around and manually executing the 'rattle()' function
at which point I get the following error: Error in rattleBM() : could
not find function "gladeXMLNew"

Does anyone have any idea what this error is? Is it GTK?? Has anyone
actually managed to get this package running on a mac??? The togaware
site only has Windows instructions :(

-Dan

Hi Daniel,

We have been looking at the issue of Rattle on Mac OSX. It seems to be a
problem, and I have no examples of anyone succeeding! I'll make note in
the web pages. You seem to almost be there though!

After the "library(rattle)" command, it is correct that "nothing"
happens. This is as it should be, since the rattle package provides
functionality that can be used outside of the rattle GUI. You do need to
the run the command "rattle()".

The fact that "rattleBM()" can't find gladeXMLNew might be because you
need the developer version of GTK2, which seems to be the one that
includes Glade (this seems to be the case for Windows). Is there a
"developer" version of GTK2 for Mac OSX from where you obtained your
version? I'd be hopeful that that would help.

Please let me know how you go, as I don;t have access to Mac OSX.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Rattle on OSX
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Graham,

Your post was very helpful; I was missing Glade (libglade2
specifically). I installed it via darwinports but rattle still died
while trying to invoke gladeXMLNew. To get things working I had to
remove RGtk2 and recompile/reinstall; the problem was that because
glade was missing the bindings for it were not compiled into the
library.

So, after all that, I'm happy to report: Success!

Here's a rundown of the order in which things need to be installed:

GTK2 (>= 2.8.0)
libglade (>=2.5.1)
RGtk2
rattle

To make it even easier, here's a rundown of my installs via port (I
assume that the user has darwinports installed on their machine).

sudo port install gtk2
sudo port install libglade2

I had to manually download and install RGtk2 via the Terminal by doing:

R CMD INSTALL <rgtk2 file>

I was unable to compile RGtk2 via the R GUI as the GTK libraries could
not be located when gcc is called. I'm not entirely sure what the issue
was here and I didn't have the patience to chase and resolve it. Once
installed R has no problems detecing the package; just don't try to
load it within the GUI as GTK is not a native OSX application and it
will break.

I installed rattle in the same way, ie. R CMD INSTALL <rattle source
file>

To get up and running first make sure Apple X11 is installed on your
machine as GTK2 (and anything built with it) is not native to OSX.
Start R as per normal in the X11 terminal and load rattle as per
normal.

I hope this proves helpful to others!

-Dan

messages.subject: Feature request
messages.body_plain:
I'd like to throw in a request for a new feature: A missing values tab

Some of the algorithms seem to have a problem handling missing values.
There are several methods for dealing with missing values that would
fit nicely in the tab-style of Rattle.
